title: The Only Vertebrate With Clear Blood Lives in Freezing Antarctic Water
subject: icefish

scenes.text: There's a fish whose blood is clear. And it has no red blood cells at all.
The icefish is the only vertebrate on Earth without red blood cells or hemoglobin.
Its blood carries less than ten percent of the oxygen of its red-blooded relatives.
So how does it live? It has a much bigger heart, and wider blood vessels.
The water around Antarctica is so cold it can drop below the freezing point of blood.
The cold water holds lots of oxygen, so these fish are pale, ghostly, and still thriving.

description:
The Antarctic icefish has clear blood with no red blood cells, the only vertebrate known without hemoglobin.
Its blood carries less than ten percent of the oxygen of its red-blooded relatives, so a bigger heart does the work.
What other animal breaks the rules of biology?
first_comment: Icefish hearts use about twice as much energy to do the same job. Would you trade red blood for clear?
